name: Piper PA-31T Cheyenne
summary: Piper's pressurized twin turboprop derived from the PA-31 Navajo airframe, with PT6A engines and a long pointed nose.

wings: Wingtip fuel tanks on most examples
engines: Two PT6A turboprops in long nacelles with exhaust stubs
Three-blade propellers, with the nacelles stretching well ahead of the wing
fuselage: Navajo-like fuselage with a long pointed nose
Row of large rounded-square cabin windows
Door with airstair at the rear left
tail: Swept fin with a dorsal fillet

tellTales: Low-wing twin turboprop with a long pointed nose and Navajo-style cabin
Wingtip fuel tanks on most examples
Low horizontal tail (not a T-tail) with exhaust stubs from long nacelles

confusedWith.howToTell: The Navajo has piston-engine cowlings and a blunter nose; the Cheyenne has smoother turbine nacelles, prop spinners and a longer pointed nose.
The PA-42 Cheyenne III/400 is longer with a T-tail; the PA-31T has a low horizontal tail.
The King Air 90 has a rounder nose and a larger, airliner-like cabin without tip tanks; the Cheyenne has a long pointed nose and usually wingtip tanks.
